title: 人生就是一场赶车
source: 王德峰 为什么人到四十不信命，就是悟性太差？ https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV15h4y1r7qH?vd_source=a540eabadc07c76d83727759789f2efd
summary: 从一次追赶 166 路公交车的经历，思考天赋、目标、努力与运气：机会到来时，先让自己在场。

items.note: 出校门-西北门就是科大东区车站，离得很近。
如果没有清晰的目标（赶上 166 路车），那也不会奔跑。

我打算去银泰迪卡侬买一件衣服，在东区 1958 咖啡馆忙完事后，看到车距仅剩 1 分钟 2 站。
但是我事已经做完，所以没有选择等下一班的 20 分钟，而是选择立刻起跑。
校门口恰好的绿灯，和路口正在等候红灯的 166 路车。

items.text: 如果我不奋力奔跑，那个恰好的绿灯对我毫无意义，它会像以往一样变红。
运气是给赶路人准备的捷径，而不是给观望者预留的空位。
运气负责在那一刻给你机会；而努力，负责让你在那一刻，刚好在场。

en.title: Life is a race to catch a bus
en.summary: A sprint to catch the No. 166 bus becomes a reflection on talent, goals, effort, and luck: when an opportunity arrives, be there to meet it.
en.source_title: Wang Defeng: Why does not believing in fate at forty suggest a lack of understanding?

items.note: The USTC East Campus bus stop is just outside the northwest gate, very close by.
Without a clear goal, catching the No. 166 bus, I would not have started running.

I planned to buy a piece of clothing at Decathlon in the Intime shopping mall. After finishing my work at the East Campus 1958 café, I saw that the bus was only one minute and two stops away.
Since my work was already done, I chose to start running immediately rather than wait twenty minutes for the next bus.
The light at the campus gate happened to be green, while the No. 166 bus was waiting at a red light at the intersection.

items.text: If I had not run as hard as I could, that perfectly timed green light would have meant nothing to me. It would have turned red, just as it always did.
Luck is a shortcut for people already on their way, not a reserved seat for those watching from the sidelines.
Luck gives you an opportunity at a particular moment; effort makes sure that, at that moment, you are there.
